name: Tessera TKR-SL 'Inquisitor'
description:
The Tessera TKR-SL is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum with BCI smart-link integration and Tessera's full biometric authentication suite. The weapon represents Tessera's entry into the smart-linked revolver market — a direct competitor to the Arcturus Warden that emphasizes Tessera's ecosystem integration over Arcturus's raw performance.

The Inquisitor's smart-link system is tightly integrated with Tessera's corporate security network. In addition to standard ballistic overlay and round-count tracking, the weapon feeds firing data — including time, location, direction, and target information — directly to Tessera's security monitoring infrastructure in real time. Every shot fired by an Inquisitor is logged, time-stamped, geo-tagged, and archived. Tessera markets this as 'accountability assurance.' Critics call it surveillance.

The technical performance is excellent — Tessera's BCI protocols are mature and the .357 Magnum platform is proven. The Inquisitor shoots well, handles well, and integrates seamlessly with Tessera's broader security systems. The question isn't whether it works, but whether the operator is comfortable knowing that every trigger pull is being watched, recorded, and analyzed by their employer.
legality: Restricted — BCI registration and corponation security clearance required
specifications:
caliber: .357 Magnum
effective_range: 55 meters (smart-linked)
rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 1.08 kg
BCI_latency: <8ms
tactical_use: A smart-linked revolver with full corporate security integration. The BCI overlay provides targeting assistance and round-count tracking. Real-time firing telemetry provides command-level awareness of every discharge. The .357 Magnum platform offers reliable stopping power. The biometric lock prevents unauthorized use. Best suited for corponation security operations where individual accountability and oversight are priorities.
cultural_context: The Inquisitor crystallizes the tension between capability and control that defines Tessera's relationship with its employees. The weapon makes its carrier more effective while simultaneously making their every action transparent to the corporation. Among Tessera security personnel, accepting an Inquisitor assignment is understood as accepting a higher level of scrutiny in exchange for superior equipment.
story_hooks: An Inquisitor's telemetry data contradicts the shooter's account of a lethal incident — the weapon says it fired north, the shooter says they fired south. Either the weapon or the shooter is lying, and the implications of each possibility are different but equally disturbing.
A Tessera operative discovers that the Inquisitor's telemetry has been broadcasting to a second, unauthorized receiver. Someone outside Tessera knows every shot every Inquisitor has ever fired.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modern revolver with unmistakable corporate precision engineering. The Inquisitor presents as compact and purposeful, with clean lines and integrated tech ports along the frame. The silhouette is traditionally revolver-shaped but refined — no bulky rail systems, instead subtle access points for data connectivity. It reads as 'professional oversight' rather than 'street enforcer.'
physical_description.dimensions: 19.5 cm overall length, 13.2 cm barrel, 5.1 cm height across frame. Compact enough for duty carry but with substantial heft in the cylinder.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and authoritative in hand at 1.08 kg — not light, not heavy, but confident. The weight distribution favors the cylinder, lending stability. Single-handed control is smooth; double-handed stance is rock-solid.
physical_description.primary_material: Stainless steel frame and barrel with reinforced polymer grip module. Cylinder is aerospace-grade aluminum alloy. Internals are precision-machined steel.
physical_description.finish: Brushed stainless steel on frame and barrel with a charcoal anodized cylinder. The polymer grip panels are matte black with subtle texture. BCI access ports feature recessed brushed titanium bezels.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant brushed steel-silver with charcoal-black accents. The grip panels are matte black. Tessera's corporate teal appears as thin accent striping along the top strap and ejector rod housing.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with aggressive diagonal grip panels designed for reliability in wet or gloved conditions. The grip transitions to bare brushed steel at the trigger guard — cold, industrial touch point.
distinctive_features: Recessed BCI data port (rear frame, just above grip) with illuminated access indicator — glows soft white when powered, amber during data transmission
Minimalist rear sight with integrated optical reference point for smart-link overlay alignment
Cylinder with precision-indexed alignment marks visible when swung open — no guessing, no improvisation
Ejector rod with Tessera's Φ currency symbol micro-etched near the muzzle end
Trigger guard slightly oversized for gloved operation, with subtle checkering
Recessed hammer with anti-snag profile — designed for shoulder carry in corporate contexts
Round count indicator — small LED window on left frame showing remaining chambers (displays as white dots, dims as rounds fire)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Behavioral Exchange logo stamped cleanly on right frame (just below cylinder pin). Micro-stamped 'TKR-SL' on top strap. Serial plate on left frame with registration QR code. Corporate security certification hologram affixed to trigger guard.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate. The Inquisitor exists in corporate security arsenals where maintenance logs are as important as rounds fired. Typical field units show zero wear — protective lubricant sheen, perfect edges, pristine grip panels. This is a tracked, audited weapon. Abuse is liability.
